subject: Ironworks: intermittent outbound failures — SNAT ports exhausted & MTU fragmentation
messages:
From: Natalie Hartley <ops@ironworks.io>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T07:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Ironworks] Outbound uploads failing (S3 + payments) - started 06:30 PDT

Hi Markus / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent outbound failures from our on-prem cluster to external services around 06:30 PDT. Symptoms:
- Large numbers of TCP retransmits and resets when clients upload to S3 and POST to payment gateway.
- Some long-lived flows break after ~30-90s with RSTs.
- Our monitoring shows ephemeral port usage on our edge firewall spiking to 63k+ (we have a 64k port space).

Quick checks I ran:
- conntrack count: 64512 established entries (attached snapshot: conntrack-snapshot-aug29.txt)
- tcpdump captured at border suggests many connections are using identical source ports and then dropping (attached pcap).
- I also see multiple fragmented IP packets in the capture (mss-trace.log excerpt).

We suspect either: (A) SNAT port exhaustion on our NAT device, or (B) MTU/MSS-induced fragmentation causing some middleboxes to drop fragments (we have GRE overlays for some tenants).

Can Redwood confirm whether any SNAT pooling behavior or egress clustering changes happened in-hosted/private runtime this morning? Also any recommendations for immediate mitigations (MSS clamp, temporary extra SNAT pool, or route to alternate egress)?

Attaching: tcpdump-ironworks-20260829.pcap (snippet), conntrack-snapshot-aug29.txt, mss-trace.log

Thanks — Natalie
Natalie Hartley
Network Lead, Ironworks Systems

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Hartley <ops@ironworks.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T07:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Ironworks] Outbound uploads failing (S3 + payments) - started 06:30 PDT

Thanks Natalie — adding a short triage checklist while we gather data:

1) We'll pull NAT metrics for your Private deployment and confirm SNAT port allocation and per-host port reuse patterns.
2) Karthik: can you check conntrack timeouts and whether we've had a policy change or rollout that could increase established conntrack lifetimes?
3) Vanessa: please validate routing/failover changes for Ironworks region and whether any egress cluster reassignment happened between 05:00-07:00 PDT.

Immediate steps for Ironworks ops: if possible, run tcpdump on both sides of your firewall (border and inside egress box) for 30s during a failing upload and share timestamps. If MTU/GRE overhead is present we should see MSS clamp defeats and fragmented packets with DF bits clear.

Natalie — I suggest as an emergency mitigation: lower conntrack timeout for CLOSE_WAIT/ESTABLISHED temporarily and enable MSS clamp at the egress (1350) to avoid fragmentation. If SNAT port exhaustion is confirmed we can provision a temporary secondary SNAT pool.

I'll escalate to infra and routing and we'll update within 30 minutes.

Thanks, Markus. Attached the tcpdump and conntrack snapshot. Excerpts below (sensitive lines redacted):

--- conntrack-snapshot-aug29.txt ---
...
tcp 6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.12.8.45 dst=52.216.12.3 sport=44320 dport=443 [ASSURED] ...
udp 17 29 src=10.12.8.0 dst=8.8.8.8 sport=123 dport=53 ...
(total entries: 64512)
--- end ---

--- mss-trace.log ---
Observed TCP options: MSS 1460 but IP packet shows fragmentation after GRE encapsulation (~+42 bytes), DF cleared in some fragments. Some middleboxes appear to drop fragments for HTTPS flows to payment-gateway.pay.
--- end ---

Notes: our border firewall is a third-party appliance (vendor: FortisEdge FWX). It will share SNAT pools across tenants and its port allocation policy is per-src-ip then port-range. When ephemeral ports spike to ~63k we start seeing reuse and collisions.

Can Redwood confirm: does the private runtime perform any additional SNAT (double NAT) for egress on top of customer-managed NAT? We want to rule out double translation causing port reuse anomalies.

If you can provision a temporary alternate egress path (dedicated NAT gateway or separate virtual router) that would help isolate whether it's our firewall or an upstream problem.

Thanks — Natalie

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Hartley <ops@ironworks.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Ironworks] Outbound uploads failing (S3 + payments) - started 06:30 PDT

Natalie — thanks for the artifacts, they were very helpful. Summary + recommended mitigation plan (immediate -> 24h):

Summary of findings:
- conntrack snapshot and tcpdump confirm very high ephemeral port usage on your border device (~64k) leading to port collisions.
- tcpdump shows GRE encapsulation + ~42 bytes overhead; without MSS clamp this pushes some flows into fragmentation and a subset of middleboxes drop fragments.
- No Redwood-hosted SNAT was intentionally changed during the incident window. Your Private deployment is configured with customer-managed NAT at the edge; we do not perform additional SNAT by default unless "egress-shared-nat" is enabled. I confirmed your tenant did not have egress-shared-nat enabled.

Immediate (within 30-60m):
1) Infra (Grace/Karthik): provision temporary secondary SNAT pool on Ironworks' virtual router (add /16 ephemeral port map) and route a copy of egress traffic through the alternate path so they stop contending for the same port range.
2) Ops (Ironworks): enable MSS clamp at egress — set to 1350 to account for GRE overhead and avoid fragmentation.
3) Karthik: reduce conntrack ESTABLISHED timeout from 3600s -> 1200s for ports originating from Ironworks CIDR to free ports faster.
4) Vanessa: open a targeted SG rule to allow ICMP fragmentation-needed (type 3 code 4) on egress to ensure PMTU discovery works across middleboxes.

Short-term (24h):
- Monitor conntrack entries and port allocation after secondary SNAT path is in place; if collisions persist we will schedule a brief cutover to dedicated egress cluster for heavy-upload subnets.
- If FortisEdge appliance has an OS patch or NAT allocation bug, coordinate appliance vendor support (Natalie, can you open an SR?).

I've created JIRA-4721 to track the actions and will update the ticket with the provisioning changes + timestamps. Please confirm once the MSS clamp and temporary SNAT path are in place and we will validate with a test upload.

If you want, I can provision a short-term fallback route that shifts Ironworks egress to a different Redwood cluster in another AZ (possible small latency impact) — this is our recommended isolation move if the vendor NAT appliance cannot be quickly fixed.

Marking urgent; will stay on this thread until stable.

—
